Goat, Cabbage and Wolf

LogicGame StrategyCounting
Game: Get the goat, the cabbage and the wolf across the river. Never leave the goat alone with the cabbage, or the wolf alone with the goat.
How to play: Click an animal on the farmer's shore to take it across, or press the boat to cross alone. Tick Hint for the next move.
Look for the math

This old river-crossing puzzle looks like a juggling act, but only sixteen possible positions exist. Checking them all tells us the shortest route and why no shorter one can work.

Why the order matters

The boat holds the farmer and just one passenger. The goat must never be left with the cabbage without the farmer, and neither must the wolf be left with the goat. So after taking the goat across, the farmer must bring it back before fetching the cabbage or the wolf. Returning with the wrong passenger undo all the progress.

Seven crossings

One winning route is: take the goat over, come back alone, take the cabbage over, bring the goat back, take the wolf over, come back alone, take the goat over. That is seven crossings, and there are exactly two routes of that length. The logic test searches every position — three yes/no animal locations and two possible shores for the farmer, 23 × 2 = 16 in all — using breadth-first search, and confirms that seven is the minimum and that every safe position has a route home.

What the applet really checks

The applet's own "finished" flag has a quirk: after the very first correct move (goat across, farmer back alone) it would report both animals eaten, even though the goat is alone on the far shore and the farmer is with the cabbage and wolf. The logic test compares that flag with the stated rules on all sixteen positions and finds this one wrong call; this port follows the rules on the page. The original loaded little GIF pictures of the animals; here they are simple icons, and Hint names the next crossing instead of drawing a cube of alternatives.

Use Hint once, then try to finish without it. Can you find the second seven-crossing route?
